newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INTERVIEW-GFSA says early days on price.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-GFSA says early days on price.

text.p: Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd said on Thursday it was not possible to say what, if any, price premium would be needed for New Africa Investment Ltd (Nail) to secure a key stake in the group.
"From our side we have minority shareholders for whom we have to do whatever is in their best interests," chief executive Alan Wright told Reuters.

Asked if this meant the company was looking for a premium, he said: "I wouldn't even say we are that far down the road in the negotiations that we could say we are looking for a premium...We are just at the situation where we have agreed to talk."
Nail aims to buy an effective 17.2 percent stake in Gold Fields, giving it shared control with tobacco-to-mining conglomerate Rembrandt Group Ltd which already holds a similar stake.

"We are talking about a rearrangement of a partnership. We think the parties will bring value-added to Gold Fields. We are coming from diverse areas and we have different strengths and we have different weaknesses."
Commenting on suggestions that Rembrandt might look to wind down its holding in future, Wright said:
"It has to be a possibility but my understanding is we have had a very good partnership with Rembrandt for 10 years and they have shown to be long-term, serious investors."
Gold Fields shares were last trading 9.25 rand higher at 119.00.
